sources.title: Inequality declined in the Bronze Age city of Mohenjo-daro
sources.access: publisher full HTML read and preserved
sources.observation: Residence areas digitised from early excavation plans support a diachronic inequality analysis. The regional reference is c.2600–1900 BCE; this paper does not provide the new wall radiocarbon dataset.

adversarial_checks.question: Does 3300 BCE identify a directly measured foundation date?
adversarial_checks.result: The inspected participant attribution ties the older range to ceramic comparison; the attributed charcoal range is younger and the deepest deposits are described as undated.

adversarial_checks.question: Does an earlier local occupation invalidate the regional Mature reference?
adversarial_checks.result: A local Early occupation and a regional c.2600–1900 BCE phase can coexist. No manuscript-wide chronology change is supported by the inspected material.

adversarial_checks.question: Is the 2026 Antiquity paper the new dating publication?
adversarial_checks.result: No. Its methods concern digitised residence areas and Gini coefficients.

adversarial_checks.question: Are multitemporal remote sensing and the Nal route new proposals here?
adversarial_checks.result: The 2024 primary studies provide explicit precedents. The defensible extension is dated sampling of mapped channel junctions and related occupation surfaces.

adversarial_checks.question: Can the stated 50 percent charcoal interval replace a full calibrated result?
adversarial_checks.result: No original calibration distribution was inspected. The attributed interval is retained as an access-limited report rather than a revised settlement chronology.

redistribution: Authored summaries and metadata only. Downloaded HTML and Crossref payload remain local under the RECENT_ prefix. No report pages, images or full article text are embedded in this register.
